description: Replace n=256 and both n=512 regimes with an owner-computes SM100 supernode engine. Use TMA-staged 128-wide tiles, cluster multicast, TMEM FP32 accumulators, persistent matrix/tile scheduling, and device dependency epochs so batch16 does not launch only one CTA per matrix and batch640 avoids repeated factor-sidecar traffic.

Added a graph-captured 64x64 owner-computes N=512 DAG with parallel factor, panel-solve, and triangular-update tile owners plus FP16 sidecars/FP32 MathDx accumulation. Build and official validation passed, but the first full benchmark produced no output for 962.967 seconds and was terminated, indicating first-use compilation or execution hung before a metric.

Folded the standalone factor dispatch into stage-0 panel owners, reducing first-use compilation from more than 963 seconds to 202 seconds while retaining parallel tile ownership. Official validation passed, but both ranked N=512 cells returned NaN/Inf during the full benchmark, so no metric was emitted.

Added synchronized finite checks after each owner epoch. The full benchmark localized corruption to solve-0, before any Schur-update epoch: factor/panel owners produced a non-finite output immediately for batch16/N512. This rules out sidecar indexing and later update scheduling as the first fault.

Replaced the stage-0 32-copy paired cp.async transaction with two independently committed 16-copy tile groups and removed diagnostic synchronization. Both N=512 benchmark cells still produced NaN/Inf, so transaction-group size alone did not repair the initial owner epoch.

Replaced every new N=512 FP32 cp.async tile load with the retained coalesced scalar owner-load pattern while retaining MathDx factor/TRSM/GEMM and async half sidecars. Both N=512 cells still produced NaN/Inf; the new global-leading-dimension async mover is therefore not the root cause.

Counted non-finite values independently after solve-0: the stored 64x64 factor had zero non-finite values, while every one of the seven panel tiles had all 65,536 batch16 elements non-finite. The first failure is therefore the combined POTRF-to-TRSM owner kernel, not factor storage or later Schur updates.

Separated POTRF publication from TRSM using the update-owner dispatch as epoch 0, then ran parallel panel/update owners. Full validation and benchmark passed at 691.790 us; batch16/N512 improved from the observed 508.062 us parent run to 175.995 us, while batch640/N512 regressed from 969.009 to 1095.592 us.

Kept the owner-epoch DAG only for batch16/N512 and restored the retained one-CTA persistent kernel for batch640/N512. Full validation and benchmark passed at 705.318 us; the cells measured 173.657 us and 1019.613 us respectively, but unrelated large-shape outliers raised the aggregate above Trial 6's 691.790 us.

Added a distinct batch640/N512 one-CTA-per-matrix persistent 64x64 left-looking supernode. It reads immutable source plus compact solved-panel sidecars and eliminates intermediate trailing-tile stores/epochs. Full validation passed at 697.231 us; batch640 measured 1040.472 us (best repeat 974.880 us), close to but slower than the retained high-batch path.

Overlaid the persistent high-batch factor buffer with half-update workspace, reducing dynamic shared memory from 53.3 KiB to 35.8 KiB while reloading the factor before each TRSM. Full validation passed at 707.721 us; batch640 regressed to 1206.077 us (best repeat 991.232 us), showing factor reload traffic outweighed any residency gain.

Restored resident factors and paired two 64x64 panels so each prior sidecar factor tile fed two GEMMs. Full validation passed at 723.229 us, but the 78 KiB/dual-accumulator kernel regressed batch640 to 1881.366 us, showing shared/register pressure dominated the saved factor-sidecar load.

Published the first N=256 factor through a single owner before three panel owners, removing two redundant 64x64 POTRF computations. Full validation passed at 705.260 us; N=256 measured 74.112 us (best 68.984 us), so the added dependency epoch offset the saved factor work.

Replaced N=256 with two native 128x128 SM100 MathDx supernodes across factor, panel, and rank-k/factor epochs. Full validation passed at 865.835 us, but the N=256 cell regressed from about 74 us to 1093.079 us because 64 very large-collective CTAs underutilized the device.

Compacted the retained batch640 N=512 half sidecars and MathDx shared operands from leading dimension 40 to 32, reducing sidecar/bulk-prefetch bytes by 20 percent. Full validation passed at 713.930 us, but batch640 regressed to 1317.358 us, showing unpadded shared-bank conflicts outweighed lower traffic.

Packed batch640 N=512 global sidecars at LD=32 while expanding row-wise async tile/pair/triple loads into bank-padded LD=40 MathDx shared operands. Full validation passed at a new run-wide-best 684.643 us; batch640 measured 1025.284 us and batch16 remained 179.002 us.

Best validated result: commit 0b18f368ac286b8646e796cd0736552c48e11a41 at 684.643213 us full-grid, with n256=71.474 us, batch16/n512=179.002 us, and batch640/n512=1025.284 us. The core win was a separate factor/panel/update owner DAG for batch16 (externally accepted earlier at 672.435 us public / 671.169 us secret), followed by packing batch640 global half sidecars at LD32 while retaining bank-padded LD40 MathDx shared operands. Measured alternatives: 64-wide owner DAG for both regimes 691.790 us but batch640 1095.592 us; persistent 64-wide high-batch 697.231 us / 1040.472 us; paired-panel persistent 723.229 us / 1881.366 us; unpadded compact sidecars 713.930 us / 1317.358 us; separate n256 factor epoch 705.260 us / 74.112 us; two 128-wide n256 supernodes 865.835 us / 1093.079 us. Open directions remain: use true TMA gather/scatter or swizzled descriptors to expand packed sidecars into padded shared without row-wise cp.async; build a coarse two-CTA cluster that multicast-shares one factor tile across panel owners without the 78 KiB dual-accumulator pressure; retain panel factors in TMEM across multiple Schur tiles; and test a 64-wide n256 cluster with device epochs instead of either duplicated POTRF or a serial factor-publication launch. Continue from 0b18f368 and submit it before judging the packed-sidecar gain externally.
